quote_zh: NMST (20g, 0.088mol), sodium hypochlorite (150ml, 0.222mol) and ruthenium oxide (0.5g, 0.004mol) were charged into a 500ml round bottomed flask. This mixture was heated to reflux temperature under stirring for 6-8 hours, cooled to 25-30°C and filtered. The filtrate obtained was further cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH < 3 using concentrated hydrochloric acid (54mL, 0.51mol) to form precipitated product (NMSBA). The product obtained was filtered and dried at 50°C under reduced pressure to obtain NMSBA as light yellow solid. HPLC purity >95%; Yield: 68%; and Melting point: 210-214°C.
arithmetic_check: Two mass/mole pairs are printed, two solution volume/mole pairs, a yield and no product mass. BASIS, the run's convention: the MASS-PRECISION test. Propagate the significant figures of the printed MASS to a mole interval and raise molar_mass_inconsistent only where the printed MOLE figure falls outside that interval. Both printed numbers are then treated with the precision they are actually printed with, rather than testing a rounding window on the mole figure alone. Every interval below is my recomputation, not a number the patent prints, and none of them entered any structured field of the record. RUTHENIUM OXIDE PASSES: 0.5 g is one significant figure and stands for 0.45 to 0.55 g, which at 133.068 g/mol (RuO2, RDKit from O=[Ru]=O) gives 0.003382 to 0.004133 mol; the printed 0.004 mol falls inside, so no flag. The point estimate agrees, 0.5 / 133.068 = 0.003757 mol rounding to 0.004 at the printed three decimal places. NMST FAILS: the mass is printed "20", not "20.0", so it carries two significant figures and stands for 19.5 to 20.5 g, which at 215.230 g/mol (C8H9NO4S, RDKit from Cc1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]) gives 0.090601 to 0.095247 mol, i.e. [0.09060, 0.09525]. The printed 0.088 mol lies OUTSIDE that interval, so the pair cannot be reconciled at the precision the patent prints and molar_mass_inconsistent is raised. This is the widest interval of the three NMST charges in the document, since 61.2 g and 5.0 g are each printed to three and two significant figures respectively with tighter absolute spread, and the printed figure is excluded even at this width, which strengthens the finding rather than weakening it. The same conclusion by the cruder route, kept because it is independent of the precision convention: 20 g / 0.088 mol implies 227.27 g/mol, which does not reach 215.230 g/mol, and 20 g is in truth 0.092924 mol, so the printed mole figure is about 5.3% low. Nothing corrected. CONTROLS ACROSS THE THREE STEP-(i) EXAMPLES, same compound, same mass-precision test: Example 1 prints 61.2 g / 0.278 mol, implying 220.14 g/mol, also outside its interval and also flagged on that record; Example 2 prints 5.0 g / 0.023 mol, which passes (5.0 / 215.230 = 0.02323, and the 4.95 to 5.05 g interval gives 0.02300 to 0.02347 mol, containing 0.023). So the defect is real in Examples 1 and 3, is not a convention running through the patent, and this section is the clearest failure of the pairs tested across the run. NO MASS BALANCE TEST IS POSSIBLE: the patent prints 'Yield: 68%' but no isolated mass for NMSBA, so there is no printed mass to compare against the input moles and no stated pair that disagrees; mass_balance_implausible is therefore NOT raised. For the record and NOT entered anywhere in the record, 68% of the printed 0.088 mol at 245.212 g/mol (C8H7NO6S, RDKit) would be 14.7 g, and 68% of the corrected 0.092924 mol would be 15.5 g; neither figure appears in the document. NOT MOLECULAR-WEIGHT CHECKABLE: sodium hypochlorite is charged as 150 ml with 0.222 mol (1.48 M, against Example 1's 1.49 M and Example 2's 1.49 M, so the three Examples agree on hypochlorite strength) and concentrated hydrochloric acid as 54 mL with 0.51 mol (9.44 M, identical to Example 2's 18 mL / 0.17 mol = 9.44 M and close to Example 1's 10.25 M, all plausible for a concentrated acid); both are solution volumes, not masses of substance, so neither admits a molecular-weight check and neither was flagged. STOICHIOMETRY, computed but NOT written into the record because the patent states no equivalents: on the printed 0.088 mol of NMST, hypochlorite 2.52 eq, ruthenium oxide 0.045 eq, hydrochloric acid 5.80 eq. Note the catalyst LOADING against Example 2: both charge 0.5 g of ruthenium oxide, but Example 2 does so at 5.0 g of NMST and this Example at 20 g, a fourfold difference in loading between two Examples of one procedure. Recorded as printed; no validation flag in the prompt's list covers a loading difference between sections and none was invented. PURITY IS A MEASUREMENT REPORTED AS A BOUND, NOT A SPECIFICATION: the analytical line at 289 prints 'HPLC purity >95%' (closed up, no space, unlike Example 2's '> 92%') for the single batch this Example made, so product_purity_pct is 95.0 with purity_method hplc, the inequality kept verbatim in quote_zh, procedure_text and the record notes, and 95.0 understood as that printed lower bound rather than an assayed equality. This agrees with A1, which holds purity_pct 95.0 and raw_text 'HPLC purity >95%' for the same compound. 'Yield: 68%' is likewise a measurement and is recorded; with no isolated mass printed it cannot be cross-checked against a mass. The summary section's 'at least 65%' and 'at least 85%' are specifications of the invention in general and enter no numeric field of this record. UNRESOLVED, NOT REPAIRED: p16.json's discrepancy list notes that this Example's purity and melting point are character for character Example 1's while the yield differs, a possible copy-paste in the patent. Both are recorded as printed and the question is left open.

It draws NMSBA of formula (III) plus an unlabelled 1,3-cyclohexanedione over a '+' sign, a bare solid arrow, and the enol ester of formula (II) on the right, i.e. step (ii) of the route, which is EXAMPLE 4's chemistry. p16.json records this drawing exactly once, as kind 'scheme', between_markers ['[0049]', '[0050]'], presented_as 'invention_route', and its notes state the printed position explicitly: 'sitting between the Example 4 title line and the paragraph marked with the four-digit number ending 50'. build_enriched.py anchors a drawing on between_markers[0], so the span was emitted after [0049] and thereby landed between Example 3's procedure at 285 and Example 3's own analytical line at 289. A0's note for section 11 states the same and directs A2 to attribute it to Example 4; the A1 pass for this section reached the same conclusion independently, checked it against p16.json, and recorded no SMILES alias on any Example 3 compound for that reason. Three readings agree, so this is not a judgement call. HOW IT WAS HANDLED: no second record was emitted from line 287; 1,3-cyclohexanedione and the enol ester of formula (II) appear in no compounds[] entry, no reactant_names entry and nowhere else in this record; product_name is NMSBA, taken from this section's own title line at 283 and its own prose at 285 and not from the drawn product; and the span was stripped from procedure_text per prompt rule 5h. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FLAGS: because this section has no arrow for its own transformation, reagent_written_not_drawn is NOT raised, although Example 1, which does own a step-(i) scheme labelled 'Oxidant / RuO2', correctly carries it. The flag reads 'a reagent is in the procedure but not on the arrow', and there is no arrow here; the absence of a whole drawing is a different finding from a drawing that under-specifies its prose, and asserting the flag on absence would put a false finding on the record. drawing_text_conflict is not raised for the same reason: there is no drawing of this step to contradict the prose. The bare-arrow disagreement that the p16 span does carry, an arrow with nothing above or below it against a prose paragraph naming dichloromethane, DCC and 25-30°C, is Example 4's finding to record on Example 4's record.
